Möchtest Du Dein Praktikum nutzen, um ein innovatives Unternehmen im Automobilsektor kennenzulernen?
Wir suchen für das Wintersemester 2026/2027 (ca. ab Oktober) einen Praktikanten / eine Praktikantin für unser Team!

Simi erfasst seit über 30 Jahren menschliche Bewegung, zunächst für olympische Athleten, Biomechanik-Labore und Profisportteams, heute für den Fahrzeuginnenraum.

Als hundertprozentige Tochtergesellschaft von ZF LIFETEC, einem der weltweit führenden Anbieter passiver Sicherheitssysteme (Airbags, Sicherheitsgurte, Lenkräder), entwickeln wir kamerabasierte Insassenüberwachung: eine KI, die versteht, wer sich im Fahrzeug befindet, welche Position eingenommen wird und wie die Insassen optimal geschützt werden können.

Mit den Euro-NCAP-Protokollen 2026 wird der Fahrzeuginnenraum Teil der Sicherheitsbewertung: korrekte Gurtnutzung, Out-of-Position Erkennung, Kindererkennung (CPD) und Insassenklassifizierung für adaptive Rückhaltesysteme. Die Software von Simi liefert genau dieses Insassenverständnis, damit sich adaptive Airbag- und Gurtsysteme an Größe, Haltung und Sitzposition jeder Person anpassen.
Deine Arbeit fließt direkt in diese Kette ein!

Du wirst im Zuge dieses vergüteten Praktikums Teil eines kleinen, agilen und jungen Teams und begleitest unseren gesamten Entwicklungsprozess - von der Idee und dem Prototyping über die Datenvorbereitung für ML bis hin zur Evaluation neuronaler Netze.
Du unterstützt das Prototyping- und Datenteam mit eigenen Aufgabenpaketen und übernimmst von Anfang an echte Verantwortung.

You’re an engineer who is excited to work on cutting-edge software products and solutions using state-of-the-art computer vision and deep learning.

You have a solid foundation in areas like detection, classification, segmentation, or tracking—whether through previous roles, internships, or research—and you’re eager to apply those skills in an impactful, production-focused environment. You’re curious, motivated, and ready to learn from experienced teammates.

You enjoy solving challenging technical problems, asking thoughtful questions, and collaborating with others to build high-quality software. You’re excited about contributing to the perception stack for self-driving vehicles and learning what it means to build technology for safety-critical, open-world applications.

What you’ll be doing: Contribute to the design, development, and improvement of perception components that support downstream modules within the autonomy system. Help analyze perception system performance to identify areas for improvement and participate in efforts to address them.

Work with teammates to explore creative approaches to “long-tail” challenges—for example, experimenting with synthetic data, data mining techniques, or new model architectures.

Depending on your background and interests, you may also help optimize and deploy models to the vehicle, ensuring they operate within the constraints of our onboard hardware and meet our functional requirements and interface specifications.

Dominio real de C++ y Python: Si solo armás scripts básicos, este código te va a comer vivo. Necesitamos rendimiento.
OpenCV en la sangre: Experiencia comprobable manipulando video bruto (recortes, transformaciones y pre/post-procesamiento rápido de frames).
Modelos de Inferencia (YOLO): Experiencia entrenando, ajustando y desplegando modelos de detección de objetos para que corran rápido y en tiempo real.
Supervivencia en el mundo real: Saber lidiar con streams RTSP inestables, pérdida de paquetes de red y video de cámaras de baja resolución.

s.h: Tus responsabilidades en el día a día
s.t:
Domar streams rebeldes: Vas a conectarte y mantener estables flujos de video (RTSP) provenientes de cámaras de seguridad legacy de nuestros clientes. Tendrás que lidiar con cortes de red, pérdida de paquetes y mala resolución como parte de la rutina.
Pre y post procesamiento al vuelo: Vas a usar OpenCV como navaja suiza para limpiar, normalizar y recortar frames antes de mandarlos a la red neuronal, y luego procesar esos resultados de manera eficiente.
Optimización extrema de inferencia: Tu misión es integrar modelos ligeros (como YOLO) y escribir código (Python y C++) pensado para exprimir el hardware al máximo, evitando cuellos de botella en los servidores Edge.
Código a prueba de balas: Vas a diseñar rutinas tolerantes a fallos. En el mundo real, la cámara del cliente se apaga o la iluminación cambia drásticamente; nuestro pipeline tiene que sobrevivir a eso sin colapsar.
Sincronización con el equipo: Trabajarás codo a codo con nuestros líderes de arquitectura y de hardware para asegurar que la lógica de negocio se ejecute perfectamente en producción, no solo en un entorno local de pruebas.
NVIDIA DeepStream y TensorRT: Este es nuestro motor de alto rendimiento. Si sabés exprimir una GPU con esto, tenés medio pie adentro de la empresa.
Edge Computing Físico: Haber desplegado modelos en placas como NVIDIA Jetson, o tener experiencia de campo (armar gabinetes, lidiar con hardware físico).
Infraestructura CCTV Legacy: Haber renegado alguna vez con protocolos de cámaras viejas (Dahua, Hikvision, NVRs).
Integración con GenAI: Nociones de cómo conectar pipelines de visión con APIs de LLMs (como Claude) para resolver lógica de negocio.
Somos una startup que esta en pleno desarrollo con mucha demanda de desarrollos, es la oportunidad para formar parte de nuestro equipo inicial, para crecer en simultaneo (siempre depende de tu rendimiento), la compensación es negociable, ademas de las comisiones por proyectos terminados.

Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. We don't just work in the sporting industry; we are actively changing it. Since 2006, our solutions have been leading the way in sports performance software, science, and data, in a world where 1% can literally mean the difference between winning and losing.
We work with over 5,000+ teams around the world, empowering coaches, managers and trainers in premier teams in the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS, EPL, AFL, NRL, NCAA and more. We provide the information they need to optimize athletes’ health, game-day readiness, and performance, as well as in-game tactics.
Catapult is a sports technology company that empowers professional teams to make data-driven decisions. We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success.

s.h: WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT SOLVING HARD PROBLEMS
s.t:
We are looking for a Senior Computer Vision & Tracking Engineer to drive the computer vision and real-time tracking systems at the heart of our camera-based products.
Based in London (hybrid), you will be part of a small team building the perception stack that turns vision data into athlete performance insights – from neural network inference on edge AI accelerators, to 3D object tracking, to the data science that validates and extends what our system can measure. Today, that means tracking barbell-based weightlifting with sub-rep precision; tomorrow it means general human movement.
This is a role for someone who thrives on breadth. In any given week, you might be optimizing a model for edge inference, designing a new movement analysis algorithm, or analyzing data to produce athlete profiles. You'll report to a Senior Director of Engineering and collaborate closely with our embedded platform and applications teams.
If you've built real-time perception systems that had to work reliably in the real world – on real hardware, with real constraints – this is your kind of problem.

Drive the technical direction of our computer vision and tracking domain: the full pipeline from sensor readings through computer vision, motion recognition, and metric calculation.
Train, optimize, and deploy neural networks for real-time segmentation and classification on embedded hardware, including model conversion and optimization for edge accelerators.
Extend our tracking and motion recognition pipeline to support new movements and types of analysis.
Own the reliability of the domain: analyze tracking accuracy, build quality metrics, and use data to drive improvements across the pipeline.

4+ years of software engineering experience, with significant depth in the engineering of complex systems
Demonstrated experience shipping systems to production and end-to-end ownership of them
Strong proficiency in Python and C/C++ – you're comfortable across the full stack from higher level applications to performance-critical native code.
The ability to own ambiguous problems: scoping, prototyping, shipping, and measuring.

s.h: Nice to have – and what would make you exceptional
s.t:
Computer Vision and ML experience
Deeper knowledge of the mathematics behind tracking systems: 3D geometry, state estimation, filtering, optimization.
Experience with depth cameras (structured light, time-of-flight) and 3D perception.
Familiarity with embedded Linux, Docker on ARM, and systems-level debugging.

s.h: WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE
s.t: In 6 months time… You have shipped at least one meaningful improvement to detection or tracking quality, and you have a deep understanding of the tracking system and how we might extend it.

We have amazing people. We promise you’ll work with some of the most ambitious, intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.
We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary.
We work in a collaborative yet challenging environment to consistently improve our performance, which in turn impacts our customers' performance.
Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.
We value improvement and development. We are challenging ourselves to continuously grow and become a high-performance company. That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve. There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.
Whether you’re interested in sports or not, you’ll have the satisfaction of knowing your work is supporting some of the most successful teams and athletes on the planet!
Research shows that while men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized groups tend only to apply when they check every box. So if you have what it takes, but don't meet every single point in our job ad, please still get in touch!

We would love to have a chat and see if you could be a great addition to our team. We are building the future of sports performance. Our priority is to find the brightest talent who can add to our team culture, actively contribute, and be excited about what they do.
All offers of employment are subject to Catapult's positive prehire check. To find out more, please contact the Talent Partner for this role.

Astrolab is The Lunar Operations Company. We design and build the systems and hardware the lunar economy will come to depend on — rovers, power, and data networks for sustained operations on the Moon. We are focused on the problems that must be solved before the next chapter of human exploration can scale. The Moon does not forgive untested assumptions. The people who work here know that, and they wouldn't have it any other way.
The Lead Rover Navigation and Perception Engineer will be responsible for the design, tuning, analysis, and characterization of the navigation and perception system for Astrolab ’s extra-terrestrial rovers.

The Lead Rover Navigation and Perception Engineer will work closely with the flight software team to implement and test all of the rover navigation and perception algorithms.

This position is a technical leadership position with an expectation that the lead will also be doing hands on work as part of the rover guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) team to design, characterize, and test the vehicle navigation and perception system.

The Lead Rover Navigation and Perception Engineer will devise test campaigns to be executed with real hardware in simulated and analog lunar environments and work with the team to execute the tests.
Note: Some travel may be required for this position

Lead a small team of engineers to design, characterize, test, verify, and validate localization and perception systems for extra-terrestrial rovers
Bring a navigation and perception solution from early design through flight operations on an aggressive schedule for Astrolab ’s CLV-1 lunar rover
Work closely with the software team to implement and test navigation, perception, and obstacle avoidance flight software
Ensure that extra-terrestrial rover navigation and perception solutions are robust, upgradable during flight, and practical
Devise, supervise, and execute navigation and perception system testing with real sensors and flight computers using a test vehicle operating in simulated lunar conditions
Ensure that navigation and perception system meet performance and NASA human rated spacecraft system requirements

Bachelor's degree in a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
10+ years designing, developing, and testing navigation, localization, and perception systems for rovers, autonomous vehicles, GPS-denied vehicle navigation systems, or similar autonomous or robotic platforms.
Experience with practical sensor fusion and Kalman filtering for wheeled vehicle navigation and perception, with specific experience using sensors with widely different modalities to determine robust navigation and perception solutions (e.g. IMU, lidar, radar, star tracker, etc.)

Experience designing, tuning, developing, analyzing, characterizing, verifying, and validating navigation and perception solutions for wheeled vehicles
Experience developing, testing, and characterizing obstacle detection and avoidance algorithms for wheeled vehicles
Experience dealing with real world issues that affect navigation/localization/perception system design and performance, such as invalid data, dropped packets, data latencies, blurry images, and similar
Experience supporting a navigation/localization system through the entire lifecycle, from early design through live vehicle operations
Experience in C++ and Python programming

Chief Technology Officer & Co-Founder
Location: Remote
Alloy Partners is a venture builder with a radical thesis: that we can build and scale advantaged companies in partnership with corporations and entrepreneurs.

Alloy Partners and the University of Notre Dame partnered to establish a first-of-its-kind venture studio and venture fund — the 1842 Studio and 1842 Fund — aligned with Notre Dame's mission of serving as a "Force for Good" in the world.

In close partnership with the University and its vast network of alumni, corporate, community, and academic leaders, the 1842 Studio co-creates startups that address critical societal challenges, including improving health outcomes for vulnerable patient populations.
Nurses spend much of every shift documenting care they have already delivered, manually and from memory, hours after the fact. That time competes directly with patient care, and the record it produces captures only a fraction of what actually happened in the room.

Making that care visible gives nurses back their time at the bedside and shows care teams, for the first time, an accurate picture of the care being delivered. That picture lets nursing leaders staff, train, and support their people on evidence rather than estimation.
Co-developed with a leading academic medical center, StealthCo is an ambient AI platform that transforms nursing and medical care. By deploying AI models that continuously monitor patients and care teams through existing hospital camera and sensor infrastructure, StealthCo delivers real-time protocol and actionable clinical decision support directly to nurses and physicians at the bedside.
We are seeking a hands-on computer vision architect and builder to join as CTO and Co-Founder and personally build the StealthCo platform from the ground up alongside the founding CEO. This is a builder role, not a research role. First-year output is a working pilot and a viable product — not papers, not a hiring plan, not a research agenda.
What You'll Own
Computer vision. Build detection and activity recognition that works on commercially available cameras in real clinical environments, whether a hospital already has them installed or is deploying them for the first time.
Data as the asset. Start from off-the-shelf models to move fast, then build a proprietary dataset that gets better over time. You own that pipeline end to end.
Annotation. Stand up the labeling operation and the quality bar behind it. Domain experts say what matters clinically. You decide what is reliably detectable.
Deployment. Help us architect the right distribution of technology, from cloud to on-premise. You have been through enterprise IT security review before.
Architecture. Own the technical design and set the boundaries between components so specialists can be brought in later without breaking it.
Lean resource management. You will build using an intelligent mix of your own hands-on work, AI agents, and targeted contractors — minimizing full-time headcount until revenue and milestones warrant it.
Future technical hiring. As StealthCo grows, you will help recruit and evaluate future engineering headcount growth.
Customer and investor presence. You will be in the room with the design partner's clinical and IT teams, at Seed investor pitches, and at future health system customer meetings. You need to hold substantive technical conversations across the table from a hospital IT leader or clinical informatics team and be taken seriously by them.

Hands-on computer vision experience — you have personally written model code, not only managed people who did. You can speak fluently about what models exist today for activity recognition, multi-person tracking, and pose estimation in constrained, real-world video environments, and you have built something that actually worked.
Fixed-camera video work in messy, real-world conditions — multi-person tracking, occlusion handling, activity or action recognition, and human pose estimation. Body-worn camera, workplace safety, intelligent security, surgical video, or retail computer vision experience translates directly.
A shipped product in production, not only a model. You have taken something from zero to production with a small team and real customers. Founder or early employee track record is strongly preferred.
Edge or on-premise inference deployment — you have deployed models in environments where data cannot leave the building or where strict data residency requirements apply.
Model adaptation and fine-tuning over from-scratch training — you know how to get to a working system fast using what already exists rather than building everything from the ground up.
Startup or early-stage operating experience — you have built something meaningful with a small team, made decisions without complete information, and shipped when it was good enough rather than waiting until it was perfect. You are comfortable with ambiguity and you move through it rather than waiting for it to resolve.
Minimum 10 years of relevant technical experience with demonstrated people management responsibility.
Strong Differentiators
Prior work on body-worn camera platforms, workplace safety video AI, retail computer vision, or surgical video AI — experience with real-world video in uncontrolled environments translates directly to this deployment context.
Experience at companies deploying computer vision at operational scale — Axon, Voxel, Intenseye, Protex AI, Theator, Caresyntax, Standard AI, or similar.
Chain of custody, data retention, or privacy review experience from body camera or enterprise video contexts — directly transferable to hospital IT security requirements.
Healthcare or clinical technology exposure — not required, but any prior experience navigating HIPAA compliance, hospital IT procurement, or clinical workflow integration is an advantage.
Prior founding exit — acquisition or meaningful venture-backed outcome.

Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance

## ##
The Image Processing Engineer is a technical contributor within the **Machine-Readable Features Laboratory**, supporting the **development, integration, validation, and optimization of image processing and computer vision algorithms** used in machine-readable authentication and traceability systems.
The role covers a broad range of technologies including **image analysis, machine vision, computer vision, optical sensing, signal processing, and machine learning techniques** applied to advanced security features. The position combines **algorithm development, software implementation, data analysis, system integration, and experimental validation** in close collaboration with multidisciplinary teams including optics, electronics, chemistry, software engineering, and data science.
This position is well suited for an engineer seeking to build deep expertise in image processing, industrial machine vision, and authentication technologies, while contributing to innovative security solutions from concept through industrial deployment.
## ##

* Develop, implement, and optimize image processing and computer vision algorithms for machine-readable authentication systems.
* Design and evaluate algorithms for feature detection, classification, segmentation, pattern recognition, and image enhancement.
* Analyze large image datasets to extract meaningful information and improve feature detectability and robustness.
* Support the development of algorithms for optical inspection, authentication, traceability, and quality control applications.
* Collaborate with optics, electronics, and software teams to integrate image processing solutions into embedded and industrial systems.

Optical SSA / Image Processing Engineer
This is a future role. We're building a shortlist now and will contact you when it opens.

Foundational is building the most precise picture of Earth and orbit, using lasers fired from the ground. We call it ground truth for orbit.
We design and run low-cost, autonomous satellite laser ranging stations. They measure the distance to satellites with extreme precision, day and night. Our data platform turns those measurements into tracking data and orbit products for satellite operators, space agencies and governments. We also build our own flight-proven laser retroreflector arrays, so any satellite can be tracked.
Our station network is expanding across Europe, South America, Africa and Australia. The data supports resilient navigation, Earth observation and the safe, sustainable use of space.
We're a small, fast-moving team of engineers, scientists and operators in London. We're backed by venture investors and supported by ESA, the UK Space Agency, Innovate UK and the European Innovation Council.

London · Full time · On-site
As well as ranging with lasers, our stations track satellites optically. You'll build the image processing that finds, tracks and measures objects in our camera data.

Develop pipelines for detection, streak extraction and astrometry
Calibrate cameras and timing so that measurements are accurate and traceable
Build real-time processing to support closed-loop tracking
Validate results against catalogue orbits and our own laser data
Work with the optics and software teams on camera selection and integration

A degree in physics, astronomy, computer science or similar
Image processing and computer vision in Python or C++
Astrometry and photometry experience, for example with astropy or Source Extractor
Knowledge of camera sensors: noise, calibration and time-stamping

Space situational awareness or satellite tracking
GPU processing
Machine learning for detection
Amateur astronomy
